source: Bertolotti & Mari (2025) An LLM-based Delphi study to predict GenAI evolution
finding: First LLM-run Delphi: one model plays facilitator and simulated experts; no humans.
numbers: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, temperature 0.7, 5 rounds fixed (no stop at consensus), 12 experiments varying responders (5 or 15) and responses (5 or 15).
limits: One small model, one topic (GenAI futures). No ground truth. Authors admit knowledge cutoff, bias, sensitivity to initial conditions, weak heterogeneity. Same LLM for both roles, differing only by system prompt and allowed actions.
agent_relevance: Delphi can be a loop of facilitator plus role-prompted voices, but one model gives correlated voices (G4); needs a count-based stop, not a fixed round count.

finding: Themes (geopolitical fragmentation, regulation, economic gaps) appear in some runs and not others, so output depends on the run.
numbers: Table of 12 experiments marks yes/no per theme; e.g. fragmentation is cited for experiments 1,3,4,7,9,10,12 only (7 of 12).
limits: Run-to-run variance is shown, never quantified as a statistic. Qualitative only.
agent_relevance: Single-run scenario sets are unstable; the agent should resample and count theme frequency in code.

finding: Adapted Delphi (personas, rounds, shared rationale) gives estimates that track verifiable ground truth.
numbers: Three benchmarks (BountyBench, Cybench, CyberGym); GPT-5.1 r=0.97/0.97/0.91, Claude Opus 4.1 r=0.95/0.98/0.93; MAE 4.5 to 6.1 pp; ECE 1.6 to 4.1 pp. Panel size 5.
limits: Proxy tasks only; real target quantities have no ground truth. Method suited to filling a risk model from a given evidence pack. Estimates improve as evidence is added.
agent_relevance: Strong template: elicit numbers with evidence, test on proxy tasks first, ablate evidence to check sensitivity.

finding: Model choice matters more than persona choice; open-weight reasoning models match frontier.
numbers: Barrett reproduction: personas on same model differ 2.4 pp per task in round 1, same persona across models 4.8 pp; after mediation 0.5 pp vs 4.4 pp. GLM-5 and Kimi K2.5 on par; Llama-4 Maverick (no extended reasoning) r=0.74, MAE 10.8 pp on Cybench.
limits: Contamination cannot be excluded for one reproduced study (predates cutoffs). Evidence ladder none/benchmark/model/full tested.
agent_relevance: Persona diversity is weak; model diversity is stronger. Supports G4 (no persona voters).

finding: LLM panels agree with human expert panels, sometimes closer than humans agree with each other, but spread is compressed.
numbers: Murray et al. reproduction: two human panels differ by MAD 16.6 pp; GPT-5.1 within 5.0 pp of Panel A; Opus 4.1 12.8 pp higher. Largest gap on task 'Unbreakable': LLM 51 to 61% vs human 30 to 39%.
limits: Authors: spread only partly tracks real uncertainty; first-round spread and between-model disagreement are better signals than final spread.
agent_relevance: Use disagreement between different models as the uncertainty signal, never the post-discussion spread.

source: Barrett et al. (2025) Toward quantitative modeling of cybersecurity risks due to AI misuse
finding: Human Delphi and LLM-simulated Delphi run side by side to feed Monte Carlo risk models.
numbers: 9 human cyber experts, 2 rounds with facilitated discussion for one risk model; 9 risk models in total built on MITRE ATT&CK steps; LLM estimators used at scale.
limits: Human Delphi covered one model only. Code for simulated Delphi promised, not checked. LLM probability estimates close to humans; quantity estimates (actors, attempts, impact) diverge.
agent_relevance: Scenario to model decomposition then numeric elicitation is a usable loop; LLM is conservative on quantities.

finding: LLM experts predict lower uplift and lower uncertainty than humans, gap grows with task difficulty.
numbers: Text: LLM estimators 'significantly lower' uplift; deviation from humans rises with difficulty; less uncertainty at higher AI capability. Humans: wide spread on quantity factors, narrower on [0,1] probabilities.
limits: Exact effect sizes not extracted this session.
agent_relevance: LLM tail risk is likely understated; overconfidence grows exactly where scenario work matters (extremes).

source: Csaszar, Peterson & Wilde (2026) The strategic foresight of LLMs
finding: Fully prospective tournament: frontier LLMs ranked live ventures better than experienced managers.
numbers: 30 live Kickstarter tech projects (launched after model cutoffs); 870 pairwise comparisons per ranking; vs 346 Prolific managers and 3 MBA investors. Human rank correlation 0.04 to 0.45; Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.74; GPT-5 family 0.67 to 0.71; Prolific crowd 0.19; best human 0.45.
limits: Draft not for citation; N=30 projects; significance threshold about 0.31; single platform and outcome (funds raised). Gemini vs Prolific difference 0.55, p=0.001; vs Expert 3 difference 0.29, p=0.063.
agent_relevance: Direct strong evidence that a model alone can judge business futures; supports using the model for ranking, with held-out checks.

finding: Aggregation and human-AI teams did not beat the best single model.
numbers: Frontier-trio ensemble, all-20-LLM ensemble, proprietary-only, open-only, human-only and grand ensembles all below Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.74); Gemini + GPT-5 Mini = 0.77 (+0.03, not significant); Expert 3 + Gemini = 0.67.
limits: Averaging naive; interactive collaboration not ruled out. Within-family correlations 0.80 to 0.97 (GPT-5 variants).
agent_relevance: Correlated models make naive voting weak (G4); pick best model by a held-out proxy rather than averaging.

finding: Reasoning variants and general benchmarks partly predict foresight skill.
numbers: Grok-4 fast reasoning captured 89% of value vs 42% for non-reasoning; HLE score up 1 SD ~ +0.15 correlation; regression R2 up to 0.439 with controls. Reasoning effect inconsistent across other families; Llama 3.1-8b slightly beat 70b.
limits: Small N of models; mixed results across families.
agent_relevance: Deliberation helps on outlier detection; do not assume scale or reasoning always helps.

source: Soleimani (2026) LLM-generated counterfactual stress scenarios via hybrid prompt-RAG
finding: LLM macro stress scenarios: severity comes from the prompt, not the model.
numbers: 2,420 accepted scenarios, 2 model families (GPT-5.6-luna, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), 3 runs, 30 prompt variants, 8 risk-layer ablations; prompt variant dominates every ANOVA variance decomposition; removing severity bands makes GPT recession 1.6 pp milder.
limits: Macro-to-factor mapping stipulated not estimated; G7 only; temperature fixed at 1. Repeat run differs at scenario level but aggregate multiples agree within 0.007x.
agent_relevance: Stress magnitude must be set by code or humans; model is good for narrative and sector detail only.

finding: Small model contradicts itself in numbers; narrative severity and numeric severity are weakly linked.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B is 4 to 7 times more dispersed than GPT-5.6-luna and contradicts its own stated changes in 90% of cases; retrieval and news matter only where the prompt leaves magnitude free.
limits: Authors' conclusion: use for narrative and sector elicitation around a prescribed severity path.
agent_relevance: Add a code check that stated numbers match narrative (G2/G3 style); small models need it most.

source: Frohling, Giaconia, Bogucka, Quercia (2026) Agent-supported foresight for AI systemic risks
finding: Agents run the Futures Wheel (first, second, systemic order) and broaden coverage; experts judge.
numbers: 4 AI use cases by readiness level; 30 agent runs; 86 to 110 consequences per run condensed to 27 to 47 unique risks; compared with 290 domain experts, 7 leaders, and Futures Wheel sessions with 42 experts and 42 laypeople.
limits: Human-risk sets were as low as 24% as systemic (text); agent risks rated less likely. Experts found fewer risks, less systemic but judged more likely; laypeople found more emotional, less systemic ones.
agent_relevance: Hybrid rule: agents for breadth, humans or code checks for likelihood. Futures Wheel is a ready loop for agent scenario expansion.

finding: Agent novelty ratings were moderate; human risks scored consistently low on novelty.
numbers: Novelty subdimension means about 2.99 (novelty), 3.24 (originality) for agent risks; human risks 2.64, 2.94, 2.79 (rubric scale partly inferred from extracted text).
limits: Verify rubric scale before reuse.
agent_relevance: Breadth gain is modest per item but large in count.

source: Barnett, Kieslich & Diakopoulos (2024) Generative scenario writing for policy impacts
finding: GPT-4 writes paired scenarios (before and after a policy) that humans rate as plausible and sensitive to the policy.
numbers: gpt-4-turbo; 33 scenario pairs over 11 impact types after pruning; user study n=234 rating severity, plausibility, magnitude, specificity; paired t-tests.
limits: Prompts needed tailoring per impact type; model could not adequately write some types (e.g. machine autonomy). Policy (EU AI Act Art. 50) judged effective on harms such as autonomy; no theme-level plausibility change was significant; magnitude changes only for labour, media quality, trustworthiness.
agent_relevance: Paired with/without scenarios are a usable counterfactual probe; hand-tailored prompts were needed.

finding: Multi-agent value deliberation collapses to artificial consensus; mixing different models reduces it.
numbers: 120 deliberations, 2 policy scenarios, 7 to 9B models; heterogeneous models cut first-choice concentration 70.9% to 46.1% (child welfare, p<0.001, r=0.58) and 46.0% to 22.9% (housing, r=0.50); roughly half of value conflicts 'trustworthy'.
limits: Small models; coherence judged by a model (confound acknowledged). Coherence validation by a frontier model: 46.1% to 40.8% (p=0.004) in one scenario, 22.9% to 26.6% (p=0.96) in the other.
agent_relevance: Matches Delphi weakness: groups of one model converge. Use mixed models and code counts.

finding: Failed designs: Delphi-style feedback and self-confrontation did not work with 8B models.
numbers: Counter-argument exposure destabilised 8B models (binary hold or capitulate); two rounds compounded sycophantic flips; 'Delphi v7' self-confrontation: zero vote changes in 10 runs, models just restated reasoning.
limits: Small-model finding; frontier models not tested here.
agent_relevance: Delphi feedback rounds can induce sycophancy; allow revision only from new evidence (G2).

finding: GMA: parameter matrix plus cross-consistency assessment reduces a huge space to consistent configurations; computerised since 1995 at the Swedish Defence Research Agency.
numbers: Example matrix 4x4x4x3x3x4 = 2,304 configurations; original 10-dimensional shelter matrix over 500,000; cross-consistency assessment prunes to a manageable set.
limits: Non-quantified, judgement-based consistency; no accuracy tests. Zwicky's principle of contradiction.
agent_relevance: Natural code-plus-model split: model fills pairwise consistency cells, code enumerates and prunes (G5).

finding: Cross-consistency check needs pairwise judgments between conditions, a fit for LLM batch labelling.
numbers: Per text, consistency is judged pairwise between parameter conditions, with workshop judgement in the computer-supported versions.
limits: No published LLM-morphological-box evaluation found in my searches (APIs rate-limited); gap.
agent_relevance: Gap: nobody has measured LLM consistency matrices against workshop matrices.

source: Federal Reserve Board (2009) Supervisory Capital Assessment Program: design and implementation
finding: First large supervisory stress test: common macro scenario on 19 banks, bank projections plus supervisor models.
numbers: 19 bank holding companies; about two-thirds of assets; results: $185B additional buffer needed, 10 of 19 firms short, 9 of 19 already adequate; SCAP buffer $74.6B after actions in text.
limits: Scenario designed to be adverse but not worst case.
agent_relevance: Human-built scenario, bank-built numbers, supervisor cross-check: a cross-validation model for an agent.

source: Peristian, Morgan & Savino (2010) Information value of the stress test, NY Fed SR 460
finding: Market reaction showed stress test produced information only at the results clarification event.
numbers: Announcement and methodology events: no significant abnormal returns; clarification event: positive and significant for banks with a capital gap, insignificant for others.
limits: Event study of publicly traded stress-tested banks (GMAC excluded).
agent_relevance: Scenario exercises matter when they disclose new, checkable numbers, not narratives alone.

source: Synthesis: Bertolotti & Mari (2025) vs Lorenz & Fritz (2026)
finding: LLM Delphi uses the same pipeline in both: facilitator, role-prompted experts, rounds.
numbers: Bertolotti: fixed 5 rounds, gpt-4o-mini, no ground truth; Lorenz: calibrated on 3 benchmarks with r 0.91 to 0.98.
limits: Synthesis line, no new source.
agent_relevance: Delphi in an agent loop is sound only if tied to a proxy test as Lorenz did.

source: Search gap: Kahn / RAND stories and La Prospective with LLMs
finding: No LLM study found testing Kahn-style stories or Berger's La Prospective directly.
numbers: Searches (arXiv, 4 queries in two batches; web search budget exhausted) found none.
limits: Absence of evidence from limited search; Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex rate-limited.
agent_relevance: Treat as open gap; Futures Wheel (Frohling) and generative scenario writing (Barnett) are nearest.
